message.content: {"cvss_vector":"CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:L/VI:H/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N","aivss":{"LC":"I","CP":"N","AP":"N","RH":"P","ES":"W"},"rationales":{"LC":"The entry point is the path argument of a write_file call delivered by injection or a confused request; the lab names prompt injection (S1) and fetched attacker-edited pages as the delivery route, so attacker-controlled language enters through ingested content and reaches a privileged tool-invocation path (agent-sec-lab/docs/writeups/s2-over-permissioned-tools.md:5-12, agent-sec-lab/data/web/poisoned.txt:1-7).","CP":"The write_file path writes a file at an arbitrary path but does not itself alter durable agent memory; the memory store is a separate tool (remember) and the briefing does not show this path writing to it, so no attacker-controlled context persists across sessions through this path (agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:306-310, agent-sec-lab/agent/memory.py:60-66).","AP":"The effect is confined to the initially affected component: the write_file tool function inside the agent process. The briefing shows no relay into another agent, tenant, principal or policy domain (agent-sec-lab/docs/mapping.md:28, agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:306-310).","RH":"The agent can reach the workspace .env credential file and any path the process can write, which is a reward/verification-adjacent channel, and no verified reward-hacking episode is reported in the briefing, so the proxy is reachable with zero verified episodes (agent-sec-lab/docs/writeups/s2-over-permissioned-tools.md:9, agent-sec-lab/data/workspace/.env:1-4).","ES":"The baseline offers all twelve built-in tools with unvalidated arguments, and the remote MCP manifest is re-fetched every run and trusted, with a same-named remote tool overriding the built-in; the extension surface is dynamic and unvetted (agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:20-99, agent-sec-lab/agent/loop.py:34-37, agent-sec-lab/agent/mcp_client.py:1-4).","CVSS":"The agent is a local CLI with no network listener, so the attacker needs local access or relies on a user on that system to act (AV:L, UI:P). the briefing gives no evidence of a repeatable, unattended exploit chain that reliably produces that call, so it is not automatable on the evidence shown.","technical_impact":"Partial","technical_impact_rationale":"The write_file tool creates or overwrites any file the agent process can write, including the workspace .env credential file, which is a serious integrity consequence, but the effect is limited to file content the attacker chooses and does not give total loss of protection over the system.","applicability_as_implemented":{"model_directed_goal_pursuit":true,"selects_or_sequences_actions":true,"confidence":"high","rationale":"In the vulnerable baseline the CLI runs a real Anthropic model with all twelve built-in tools, the loop lets the model emit tool_use blocks that the harness executes, and the model chooses the write_file path argument, so the model directs goal pursuit and selects actions (agent-sec-lab/agent/__main__.py:9-21, agent-sec-lab/agent/loop.py:28-38, agent-sec-lab/agent/config.py:22-23)."},"applicability_as_modeled":{"model_directed_goal_pursuit":true,"selects_or_sequences_actions":true,"confidence":"high","rationale":"The documentation describes an office assistant that reads and writes workspace files, fetches pages, sends email, calls a billing API, keeps long-term notes and makes payments, with the model choosing tool calls each turn, so as documented the agent pursues goals and selects actions (agent-sec-lab/agent/loop.py:1, agent-sec-lab/agent/loop.py:43-56, agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:20-99)."},"refusal":null}
